name: Avant-Garde Rock
about: Avant-garde rock is rock that takes its cues from the twentieth-century avant-garde: minimalism, free jazz, musique concrète and the art school. It took shape in the mid-1960s in New York and Los Angeles, with the Velvet Underground's drones and feedback, Frank Zappa's tape collage and Captain Beefheart's Trout Mask Replica, which broke blues and rock rhythm into interlocking parts. Through the 1970s it ran through Faust, Henry Cow and the Rock in Opposition circle, The Residents and This Heat, each treating the studio as an instrument and the song as something to be dismantled. Since then Swans, John Zorn, Scott Walker's late records and Xiu Xiu have kept it a living tradition, and its lesson, that noise and structure can coexist, now runs through much of underground rock.

artists.name: Captain Beefheart
artists.why: fractured blues visionary of Trout Mask Replica

artists.name: The Velvet Underground
artists.why: brought drone and feedback into rock

albums.title: White Light/White Heat
albums.why: Seventeen minutes of Sister Ray and a sleeve of pure distortion made this the founding document of noise in rock, and it still sounds dangerous.

albums.title: We're Only in It for the Money
albums.why: Zappa's razor-edited satire of both the hippies and their parents, where musique concrète and doo-wop share a side without apology.

albums.title: The Marble Index
albums.why: Harmonium drones and John Cale's bleak arrangements turned the Velvets' chanteuse into a one-woman avant-garde, decades ahead of the darkwave that followed.

albums.title: Trout Mask Replica
albums.why: Delta blues rebuilt as polyrhythmic chamber music over 28 tracks; impenetrable on first hearing and, by consensus, the genre's single most important record.

albums.title: Tago Mago
albums.why: A double album assembled from hours of improvisation in a castle, its edits and grooves set the template for everything experimental rock would borrow from Germany.

albums.title: Faust IV
albums.why: The Wümme collective at their most approachable, from the twelve-minute Krautrock to pastoral songs, with the tape-splice humour intact.

albums.title: In Praise of Learning
albums.why: Henry Cow merged with Slapp Happy for a dense, political art-rock statement, with Dagmar Krause's voice at its centre and no concessions anywhere.

albums.title: Duck Stab/Buster & Glen
albums.why: The anonymous eyeballs' most song-shaped record: short, warped nursery rhymes that are as close to pop as they ever came.

albums.title: The Modern Dance
albums.why: Synthesizer squall and David Thomas's yelp over garage rock riffs made Cleveland's avant-garage the bridge between the Stooges and post-punk.

albums.title: This Heat
albums.why: Recorded in a converted meat locker, the trio's debut moves from drum-and-loop improvisation to crushing riffs and set a bar for studio experiment in post-punk.

albums.title: Winter Songs
albums.why: Fred Frith, Chris Cutler and Dagmar Krause set medieval cathedral carvings to a cold, compressed art-song cycle that remains a Rock in Opposition touchstone.

albums.title: Deceit
albums.why: Cold War dread turned into songs, with a rhythmic violence and a tape-collage logic that was later cited by everyone from Fugazi to Radiohead.

albums.title: Naked City
albums.why: Zorn's jump-cut band flips between surf, grindcore, Ennio Morricone and country inside a single minute, the purest statement of his cartoon-logic composition.

albums.title: Torch of the Mystics
albums.why: The Arizona trio's most focused record, where imaginary Eastern folk, surf guitar and ritual chant come together in something nobody has quite imitated.

albums.title: Twin Infinitives
albums.why: A double album of narcotic rock deconstruction that is close to unlistenable in places and deeply influential on the lo-fi underground anyway.

albums.title: Tilt
albums.why: After a decade of silence the former teen idol returned with industrial textures, operatic vocals and lyrics about Pasolini, and never looked back.

albums.title: Disco Volante
albums.why: Mike Patton's circus of death metal, exotica, free jazz and Arabic scales, sequenced with real compositional care beneath the chaos.

albums.title: Soundtracks for the Blind
albums.why: The sprawling farewell of the first Swans era, folding tape loops, found voices and slow-building noise into a two-and-a-half-hour requiem.

albums.title: Vision Creation Newsun
albums.why: Osaka's noise terrorists turned to trance, tribal drumming and sunrise psychedelia, producing their most ecstatic and widely loved album.

albums.title: Fabulous Muscles
albums.why: Jamie Stewart's rawest confessions set against gamelan, broken drum machines and sudden silence; harrowing, and the band's most complete record.

albums.title: The Runners Four
albums.why: Twenty tracks of lurching time signatures and sugar-sweet melody, the San Francisco band's longest and most generous statement.

albums.title: The Drift
albums.why: Punched sides of meat for percussion, Mussolini's mistress and a donkey's bray: Walker's bleakest and most fully realised late work.

albums.title: To Be Kind
albums.why: Two hours of ritual crescendos from the reformed Swans, built live over a year of touring and the peak of their second life.

albums.title: Hellfire
albums.why: The London trio's tightest record, a prog-punk cabaret about damnation that proves the tradition still has young practitioners with chops.
